item: connecting() gives its shared library level back when its cleanup hits a MemoryError, and the swap's wait for the opens in flight re-checks every second
status: shipped (rides PR #1429 as its own commit, on the swap_window commit)
summary: The same instruction sweep as the swap window's, run on connecting()'s cleanup (the part that gives the shared level back), found the old shape `if _LOCK.shared_held_here() > before: _LOCK.release_shared()` leaving a level raised at 2 of its 3 allocating instructions (the check's call and the release's call; the counters are left out because a small-integer result is a cached object, pinned by a test). A level left raised makes every later swap_window (repair, restore, encrypt in place) refuse with LibraryBusy until restart: a named refusal of a rare operation, not a hang. Fixed: _Lock.release_shared_since(before) compares the thread's record with the value read BEFORE the take and gives the level back with no call between 'it is ours' and 'it is released'; the record is a thread-local with a class default (an attribute load, not a getattr call), which also makes shared()'s 'no call between the count and the record' comment true; the swap's own wait (exclusive) takes steps of _RECHECK_S, so the one call left after the level is back (notify_all) costs a lost wake-up one step and not the swap's deadline. tests/test_connecting_allocation_failures.py sweeps the cleanup (green; the swap that was already waiting must get through within 0.5 s), pins the release and the take structurally, and catches three mutants of the module's own source (the old pair of calls, a call before the release, a swap wait with no step). Residual, named in connecting() and in the test: the CALL of release_shared_since itself, which no code after it can protect.
